content: Cannabidiol has the potential to inhibit CYP2C9 enzyme activity. When co-administered with drugs that are substrates of CYP2C9, consider reducing the dose of the substrate and monitor the patient closely. Cefaclor reduces the levels or effects of mestranol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction is relevant only for oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. Cefadroxil decreases the levels or effects of mestranol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral hormonal forms. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are recommended. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor CYP3A substrates if co-administered, and consider increasing the dose of CYP3A substrates if needed. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases mestranol levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. However, it also decreases mestranol levels by affecting hepatic CYP2C9/10 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Elvitegravir is a moderate CYP2C9 inducer. Encorafenib affects mestranol levels by both inhibiting and inducing CYP3A4 at clinically relevant plasma concentrations. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Etravirine reduces mestranol levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Mestranol and exenatide injectable solution may interact. Oral contraceptives may reduce the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics by impairing glucose tolerance. Exenatide slows gastric emptying, potentially reducing the absorption of oral medications requiring rapid GI absorption. Advise patients to take oral contraceptives at least 1 hour before exenatide administration.
